transcript:
Header: 2026-08-19 10:00 AM PT | Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (Willow Bank - CISO), Maya Singh (Willow Bank - Head of Cloud), Ethan Park (Willow Bank - DevOps), Sophie Lane (Willow Bank - Compliance)

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough): weekly security/check-in for POC; focus on SSO/SAML timing, audit log exports, data retention windows and SOC2 artifacts; next steps to share docs and schedule VPC peering test.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time this morning. quick agenda - SSO status, audit logs/retention, SOC2 and pen test artifacts, then a quick walkthrough of how we'll collect logs during the pilot.
00:18 Daniel: thanks Alex, yes we're mainly here because compliance wants to make sure we can meet retention and auditability for the pilot - also SSO so we can use our SAML provider.
00:30 Priya: great, quick note - last week we pushed the SAML metadata endpoint to the pilot env, and we saw an issue with the NameID format; should be easy to tweak on the IdP side but wanted to flag.
00:45 Maya: yeah that one bit us, our provider defaulted to transient and we need persistent; we'll update. does Redwood support both email and persistent NameID?
00:58 Priya: we support both, and SP-initiated login works. the only wrinkle is if you require specific assertion attributes, we may need to map them - e.g., department, team, custom roles.
01:12 Daniel: and SSO session length - we need sessions to respect our SSO session policy and to expire at 8 hours for pilot users. is that configurable?
01:22 Alex: yes you can set session TTLs via the console per-role, and for pilot we can set a global TTL to match your policy. we'll document where to change that.
01:36 Sophie: about RBAC - compliance requires that we can map SAML groups to roles and restrict access to PII. do we have per-route RBAC?
01:49 Priya: we have role-based access controls for routes and deployment environments; you can map SAML groups to Redwood roles and the pilot env can be scoped to a single role so only limited users can access inference keys and logs.
02:05 Ethan: quick infra Q - for audit logs, do you push events to our SIEM or do you provide raw exports? we prefer shipping to our Splunk but also want the raw CSV occasionally.
02:18 Priya: currently we do both. we can stream logs to your syslog/HTTPS endpoint or S3 bucket (for Splunk ingestion) and provide ad-hoc exports via the console. exports include request ID, timestamp, user, model, prompt hash, latency, and tokens. note: for privacy we redact full prompt text from exports unless you opt-in and enable special controls.
02:42 Maya: about redaction - for the pilot we need full prompts for debug but compliance wants it encrypted at rest and access-gated. can we have encrypted exports with KMS?
02:54 Alex: yes, we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via KMS for data at rest in Private mode; for hosted pilot we can do envelope encryption and we also have an option to encrypt exports with your KMS key if we shared the artifacts. we'll include the exact flow in the doc.
03:15 Daniel: SOC2 - we need the attestation and evidence around change control and pen tests. do you have SOC 2 Type II and a recent penetration test?
03:27 Alex: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II in our enterprise pack, and we have a pen test executive summary. i'll share the redacted report and the controls matrix. note that some backend infra providers may be listed and you may want to validate that with your vendor team.
03:44 Sophie: also need the list of subservice orgs, and whether any third-party infra is used for logs retention.
03:52 Priya: we use cloud object storage for retention by default and list providers in the matrix; for Private deployments you can keep logs in your VPC-only S3.
04:05 Ethan: about VPC peering - can we test peering between our pilot VPC and Redwood pilot env? we'd prefer private connectivity for audit log streaming.
04:16 Alex: yes we support VPC peering for Private and for Dedicated pilots we can configure peering or a private endpoint. for hosted pilot we can set up a secure S3 delivery or a VPN tunnel. let's schedule a peering test for the end of month.
04:32 Maya: timeline - our security review board wants everything in place before the executive pilot demo on 2026-09-10. is that feasible?
04:41 Alex: yes, that timeline is realistic; key blockers are SAML mapping and audit-log exports. once we get retention windows and legal hold details we'll confirm configs.
04:55 Daniel: a question on retention windows - we have 7, 30, 90 day retention tiers and some records must be 7 years for certain accounts. how flexible are the retention policies per dataset?
05:08 Priya: retention is configurable per data type and you can set different buckets/policies; for cases requiring long-term retention we recommend Private deployment so logs and raw payloads never leave your control. but for the hosted pilot we can implement per-bucket lifecycle rules and legal hold flags.
05:28 Sophie: legal hold is important - if we need to freeze data for an investigation, can you prevent deletion even by admins?
05:36 Alex: yes, legal hold prevents deletion; we have an audit trail for actions and the hold can be controlled via requests from your compliance owner. we'll note the exact process in the playbook.
05:50 Ethan: on audit logs fields - can we get token-level cost and latency per request? we need that to reconcile pilot spend and performance.
06:01 Priya: yes the token-level breakdown is available; exports include token count and cost estimate per request, though cost mapping to your billing may be approximate for pilot.
06:13 Daniel: another compliance ask - how long do you keep service account keys? can we rotate keys automatically?
06:21 Priya: service keys can be rotated; we support short-lived keys via our token exchange and recommend using short TTL service tokens for CI/CD. we'll share recommended rotation cadence.
06:34 Maya: encryption at rest - you mentioned CMK for Private. for hosted, is customer-managed key available?
06:42 Alex: for hosted we offer envelope encryption and can support customer-provided KMS in certain enterprise configurations (requires private connector). we'll include an options matrix.
06:56 Daniel: one more - do you produce a tamper-evident audit log? our auditors prefer append-only logs with hashing.
07:04 Priya: yes we have append-only logs and can provide log integrity features; there is a small config step to enable signed log entries and a verification endpoint. we'll demo that.
07:18 Sophie: wonderful. any blockers on Redwood side?
07:22 Alex: just to get Maya's retention windows and Daniel's confirmation on which users will be in the pilot so we can set up SAML mappings; Priya will follow up on the audit log demo.
07:33 Ethan: for the peering we'll confirm firewall and IP ranges, i'll send those to Alex after the call.
07:39 Alex: perfect. quick demo now - Priya can show how an audit export looks in the console.
07:45 Priya: okay sharing screen... (minor noise) so here's the audit log page - you can filter by request id, user, model, time range, and export. export options: CSV, JSON, and S3 delivery. note: prompt text is redacted by default - you'll see a prompt_hash column and a flag "prompt_included" if enabled.
08:20 Maya: can we have an automated job that pulls that CSV daily into our Splunk?
08:25 Priya: yes you can set up an S3 delivery with lifecycle rules and your Splunk can ingest; we'll provide sample lambda or ingestion guide.
08:35 Sophie: about evidence - can you provide change control logs for the pilot? we need to see who changed config during pilot windows.
08:44 Alex: change control logs are part of the audit events and will show user, change type, before/after snapshots where applicable.
08:52 Daniel: any chance to run a small pen test with our vendor? we might want to include Redwood in our scope.
08:59 Alex: we can coordinate - we'll share the pen test contact and the standard process for scoping and whitelisting IPs and test windows.
09:10 Priya: last thing - for debugging we're happy to enable prompt capture for a small set of users under an NDA; otherwise we can provide hashed prompts and replicate behavior with synthetic prompts.
09:23 Maya: that should work for now, we'll start with hashed and enable full capture for one sandbox user.
09:30 Alex: great. recap of next steps - Alex share SOC2 + pen test summary, Priya demo artifacts and export examples, Maya provide retention windows, Ethan send IP ranges and service account requirements. schedule VPC peering test for end of month.
09:48 Daniel: thanks all, this was helpful.
09:52 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the docs and DRA ticket.
09:58 End.
